Re-track cycles using a Monte-Carlo simulation

Source: R/retrack_wt_MC.R
retrack_wt_MC.Rd

When analysing multi-proxy records an age-model can be created for each proxy. These age-models can be in general agreement but might also indicate conflicting deposition rates. Picking one age-model out of the all multi-proxy age-models and stating that, that age-model is the best overlooks the information contained within the other proxies and hence a degree of error remains the age-model exists.To combine the multiple age-models all the age models can be averaged out and the uncertainty can be calculated by means of the standard deviation. The result is an age-model which takes into account all the age-models from the proxy records. The averaged out age-model does not take into account any small user errors during the creation of the individual age-models nor does the averaging take into account the differences between the age-models and how the initial age-model of a certain proxy might be off in certain intervals. the retrack_wt_MC mitigates these problems by re-tracking periods of astronomical cycles in the wavelet spectra. The re-tracking is based on the information provided by the age-models constructed from the different proxy records. First a synthetic tracked curve is created by adding up fractions (0-1) of the tracked periods of the different proxy records. This synthetic curve is then used to re-track the period/spectral peaks of an astronomical cycle in a randomly select wavelet scalogram. This process is repeated x times. The result x tracked curves which take into account all the original age-models. From the re-tracked curves one can calculate the mean period and the standard deviation. The resulting standard deviation is a good indicator of the quality of the imprint of of astronomical cycles in the proxy records. A small standard deviation indicates that given the input of the different tracked cycles similar periods keep on being tracked indicating the an astronomical is well recorded in the proxy records and as such the age-model is very reliable in set interval. A high standard deviation on the other hand means that the tracking results in vastly different periods of the tracked astronomical cycle, as such the quality of the imprint of the astronomical cycle proxy records is poor and hence the age-model is less-reliable in this interval.

Usage

retrack_wt_MC(
  wt_list = NULL,
  data_track = NULL,
  x_axis = NULL,
  smoothing = c("auto"),
  nr_simulations = 50,
  seed_nr = 1337,
  verbose = FALSE,
  genplot = FALSE,
  keep_editable = FALSE,
  create_GIF = FALSE,
  plot_GIF = FALSE,
  width_plt = 600,
  height_plt = 450,
  period_up = 1.5,
  period_down = 0.5,
  plot.COI = TRUE,
  n.levels = 100,
  palette_name = "viridis",
  color_brewer = "viridis",
  periodlab = "Period (metres)",
  x_lab = "depth (metres)",
  add_avg = FALSE,
  time_dir = TRUE,
  file_name = NULL,
  run_multicore = FALSE,
  n_cores = NULL,
  output = 1,
  n_imgs = 50,
  plot_horizontal = TRUE,
  empty_folder = FALSE,
  colour_brewer = NULL
)

Arguments

wt_list

Wavelet scalograms of the different proxy records (required): a list of objects created with analyse_wavelet, one per proxy, in the same order as the columns of data_track. In every simulation one of them is picked at random and the cycle is re-tracked in it. Default=NULL.

data_track

Tracked periods of the cycle in each proxy record (required): numeric matrix with one column per proxy (same order as wt_list) and one row per value of x_axis; contains only the period values, not the depth axis. Build it with cbind from tracked curves that were interpolated to the same depths. Default=NULL.

x_axis

Depth/time values of the rows of data_track (numeric vector, evenly spaced, same length as nrow(data_track)). Required. Default=NULL.

smoothing

Smoothing of every re-tracked curve (character vector of length 1 or 2):

  • "auto": loess smoothing with an automatically selected span (loess_auto),

  • c("loess", span): loess smoothing with the given span (0 to 1; smooth of astrochron::noLow),

  • c("window", length): moving average with the given window length in depth/time units (win of astrochron::mwStats).

Any other value applies no smoothing. Default=c("auto").

nr_simulations

Number of Monte Carlo simulations (re-tracked curves) (integer, > 0). Default=50.

seed_nr

Seed of the random number generator (integer), so that the random choice of scalogram and of the weights of the synthetic curve can be reproduced. Default=1337.

verbose

Show the progress of the simulations (logical, TRUE or FALSE). Default=FALSE.

genplot

Plot the mean re-tracked period (green) with the mean minus (red) and plus (blue) one standard deviation of the frequency (logical). Default=FALSE.

keep_editable

Keep the graphical parameters of the plot after the function returns, so that extra elements can be added (logical); only used with genplot = TRUE. Default=FALSE.

create_GIF

Save one image per simulation, showing the re-tracked curve on the selected scalogram (drawn with plot_wavelet), in the folder file_name and join them into an animated GIF (logical; needs the magick package). Default=FALSE.

plot_GIF

Display the GIF after it is created (logical); only used with create_GIF = TRUE. Default=FALSE.

width_plt

Width of the GIF images in pixels (integer). Default=600.

height_plt

Height of the GIF images in pixels (integer). Default=450.

period_up

Factor (numeric, > 1) by which the synthetic tracked curve is multiplied to get the upper boundary of the search window for the nearest spectral peak (passed to completed_series). If no peak is found within the window the interpolated value is used. Default=1.5.

period_down

Factor (numeric, between 0 and 1) by which the synthetic tracked curve is multiplied to get the lower boundary of the search window for the nearest spectral peak (passed to completed_series). Default=0.5.

plot.COI

Draw the cone of influence on the scalograms of the GIF images (logical); only used with create_GIF = TRUE. Default=TRUE.

n.levels

Number of colour levels of the scalograms of the GIF images (integer, > 1). Default=100.

palette_name

Name of the colour palette of the power (colour) scale, a character string. Which names are valid depends on color_brewer:

  • color_brewer = "grDevices": "rainbow", "heat.colors", "terrain.colors", "topo.colors", "cm.colors", or any of the 115 hcl.colors palettes (list them with grDevices::hcl.pals()), for example "viridis", "Plasma", "Inferno", "YlOrRd", "Spectral", "Blue-Red", "Zissou 1".

  • color_brewer = "viridis": "viridis", "magma", "inferno", "plasma", "cividis", "rocket", "mako", "turbo".

  • color_brewer = "RColorBrewer": "BrBG", "PiYG", "PRGn", "PuOr", "RdBu", "RdGy", "RdYlBu", "RdYlGn", "Spectral", "Accent", "Dark2", "Paired", "Pastel1", "Pastel2", "Set1", "Set2", "Set3", "Blues", "BuGn", "BuPu", "GnBu", "Greens", "Greys", "Oranges", "OrRd", "PuBu", "PuBuGn", "PuRd", "Purples", "RdPu", "Reds", "YlGn", "YlGnBu", "YlOrBr", "YlOrRd" (also listed by wr_brewer_palettes()).

  • color_brewer = "colorRamps": "blue2green", "blue2green2red", "blue2red", "blue2yellow", "cyan2yellow", "green2red", "magenta2green", "matlab.like", "matlab.like2", "ygobb".

  • color_brewer = "scico" (all except "batlowK" need the scico package): "acton", "bam", "bamako", "bamO", "batlow", "batlowK", "batlowW", "berlin", "bilbao", "broc", "brocO", "buda", "bukavu", "cork", "corkO", "davos", "devon", "fes", "glasgow", "grayC", "hawaii", "imola", "lajolla", "lapaz", "lipari", "lisbon", "managua", "navia", "nuuk", "oleron", "oslo", "roma", "romaO", "tofino", "tokyo", "turku", "vanimo", "vik", "vikO".

Low power is drawn with the first colour of the palette and high power with the last. Default="viridis".

color_brewer

Palette family from which palette_name is taken, a character string: "grDevices", "viridis", "RColorBrewer", "colorRamps" or "scico" (the last one, except for "batlowK", needs the scico package). See palette_name for the palette names of each family. Default="viridis".

periodlab

Label of the period axis of the plots (character). Default="Period (metres)".

x_lab

Label of the depth/time axis of the plots (character). Default="depth (metres)".

add_avg

Draw the average wavelet power next to the scalograms of the GIF images (logical; passed to plot_wavelet); only used with create_GIF = TRUE. Default=FALSE.

time_dir

Direction of the depth/time axis in the GIF images (logical): TRUE if time increases with increasing depth/time values (e.g. a core that gets older downwards), FALSE if it decreases (e.g. a section log where 0 m is the base); only used with create_GIF = TRUE. Default=TRUE.

file_name

Name (character) of the folder created in the working directory for the GIF images, also used as the base name of the images (file_name_<simulation number>.jpeg) and of the GIF (file_name.gif). Required when create_GIF = TRUE. Default=NULL.

run_multicore

Run the Monte Carlo simulations in parallel on several cores (logical). Default=FALSE.

n_cores

Number of cores used when run_multicore = TRUE (integer, or NULL). NULL uses an automatic, safe number: physical cores minus one, at most 4, and limited by the free memory; set options(waverider.n_cores = ...) to change it. A value > 1 also switches on parallel computing. Results do not depend on the number of cores. Default=NULL.

output

What is returned (integer, 1 to 7):

  • 1: list of (1) a matrix with the x-axis, the mean tracked frequency and its standard deviation (columns depth, mean_freq, sd), (2) a matrix with all the re-tracked periods (one column per simulation) and (3) the GIF (NULL without create_GIF = TRUE),

  • 2: list of the mean/sd matrix and the matrix of re-tracked periods,

  • 3: list of the mean/sd matrix and the GIF,

  • 4: list of the matrix of re-tracked periods and the GIF,

  • 5: the mean/sd matrix only,

  • 6: the matrix of re-tracked periods only,

  • 7: the GIF only.

Default=1.

n_imgs

Number of images (simulations) put in the GIF (integer, > 0; at most nr_simulations). Many images take long to process and give a large GIF. Default=50.

plot_horizontal

Orientation of the scalograms of the GIF images (logical): TRUE puts depth/time on the x-axis, FALSE on the y-axis. Default=TRUE.

empty_folder

Delete all files in the folder file_name before the new images are written (logical); only used with create_GIF = TRUE. Default=FALSE.

colour_brewer

British spelling of color_brewer, with the same options; if given (not NULL) it overrides color_brewer. Default=NULL.

Value

The output depends on the output setting If genplot = TRUE a plot will be generated in which the mean period and standard deviation is plotted if plot_GIF = TRUE a GIF with n number of n_imgs will be plotted in which the retraced curve is plotted in a wavelet scalogram If output = 1, output is a list which contain 3 objects. object 1 is a matrix with the x-axis and the mean tracked frequency and standard deviation. object 2 is a matrix with all the tracked periods. Object 3 is a GIF in which all the tracked periods are plotted. If output = 2, output is a list which contain 2 objects. object 1 is a matrix with the x-axis and the mean tracked frequency and standard deviation. object 2 is a matrix with all the tracked periods. If output = 3, output is a list which contain 2 objects. object 1 is a matrix with the x-axis and the mean tracked frequency and standard deviation. Object 2 is a GIF in which all the tracked periods are plotted. If output = 4, output is a list which contain 3 objects. Object 1 is a matrix with all the tracked periods. Object 2 is a GIF in which all the tracked periods are plotted. If output = 4 output is a list which contain 3 objects. Object 1 is a matrix with all the tracked periods. Object 2 is a GIF in which all the tracked periods are plotted. If output = 5 a matrix with the x-axis and the mean tracked period and standard deviation is returned. If output = 6, a matrix with all the tracked periods is returned. If output = 7, a GIF in which all the tracked periods are plotted is returned

Examples

# \donttest{
# Re-track the 110kyr eccentricity cycle in the wavelet scalogram
# from the XRF record of the Bisciaro data set of Arts (2014)

Bisciaro_al <- Bisciaro_XRF[, c(1, 61)]
Bisciaro_al <- astrochron::sortNave(Bisciaro_al,verbose=FALSE,genplot=FALSE)
#>  * Duplicates found
#>  * Duplicates values will be averaged.
#>  * Number of samples post-averaging= 287 
Bisciaro_al <- astrochron::linterp(Bisciaro_al, dt = 0.01,verbose=FALSE,genplot=FALSE)
Bisciaro_al <- Bisciaro_al[Bisciaro_al[, 1] > 2, ]

Bisciaro_al_wt <-
 analyse_wavelet(
   data = Bisciaro_al,
   dj = 1 /50 ,
   lowerPeriod = 0.01,
   upperPeriod = 50,
   verbose = FALSE,
   omega_nr = 8
 )
